items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: That's slower Don than a friend of mine used to preach to you.

ctx.x: Then I gather, well, like up in Chicago, you know, things started drying up a lot. I mean, it started.

Yeah, things started drying up around about, let's see, around, around, about, in the mid-forties, 45 or 46. Mm-hmm. I stopped playing with the most guys to stop, and I had a second wife there. And I went, I got a job in the lawn, just sorting out clothes, and I got to be what they call a spotter. That's slower Don than a friend of mine used to preach to you. He had a beautiful voice. And, can't think his name right now, he was working at a founder where he made the foam plows, you know. And I was scared when I…
But you were playing a little bit of music on his side?
